# Retrospective — {scope: weekly · cycle · wave} — {YYYY-MM-DD}

**Scope:** Weekly · Cycle · Wave
**Period covered:** {start → end}
**Facilitator:** {name}
**Participants:** {names}

> Use the same template for weekly Three-Ls retros, end-of-cycle retros, and end-of-wave retros. Scope determines depth — a weekly retro might be 30 minutes; a wave retro might take a full day.

---

## 1. Three Ls

### Liked
What went well? What should we keep doing? Concrete examples beat generic praise.

- ...

### Learned
What did we discover? Surprises, dead ends, "huh, didn't expect that" moments. These are the highest-value bullets — capture them carefully.

- ...

### Lacked
What was missing? What got in the way? Phrase as gaps, not blame.

- ...

## 2. Metrics

- **Throughput:** ...
- **Cycle time:** ...
- **Spillover:** ...
- **DoR / DoD compliance:** ...
- **(Wave retros only)** Wave-level metrics: items shipped, ADRs created, contributors involved, scope creep vs. shaping accuracy

## 3. Decisions taken in this retro

Not every retro produces decisions, but the ones that do should record them clearly. Decision-worthy items get promoted to ADRs (`../architecture/decisions/`).

- {decision} — {rationale}

## 4. Process changes

If anything in `../planning/PROCESS.md` should change because of what we learned, name it here. PROCESS.md changes are work items themselves (`type:process`).

- {change} — {why}

## 5. Action items

Concrete follow-ups. Each has an owner and lands in the backlog.

- [ ] {item} — owner: {name}
- [ ] {item} — owner: {name}

## 6. (Wave retros only) Wave transition

When closing a wave: confirm the wave-completion trigger (`../planning/PROCESS.md` §6) — wave retro done, ecosystem roadmap updated, next wave's items unlocked to advance past Level 2.
